page: Microsoft Azure D2as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dasv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It features 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or a GPU, but it is Premium Storage capable and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core capabilities are highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Conversely, multi-core and overall throughput metrics are limited by the 2-vCPU hardware profile. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU score, and static web serving throughput are classified in the weak category (bottom 25%). Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, while small-block cached read bandwidth is weak.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the D2as_v7 is defined by its low resource footprint and strong single-threaded execution. It offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads that require high single-core performance but do not scale across multiple threads. However, the lack of local storage and the weak multi-core performance present clear tradeoffs for resource-intensive applications. This server is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded processing tasks, basic web serving, and small-scale development or testing environments.
